summary: Executed backend+frontend regression for payment defaulting, deferred journal behavior, four-eyes approvals, and login/financial-control smoke. Core requested business flows passed; one auth/CORS security misconfiguration remains.

critical.issue: CORS can return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * while credentials are enabled. This violates browser CORS credential rules and may break credentialed auth flows in strict clients.

action_items: Fix CORS origin reflection for credentialed requests: never emit '*' when allow_credentials=true; return explicit matched origin only.
Re-run auth playbook checks after CORS fix to fully verify brute-force lockout + bcrypt assertion path in one green run.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has dual CORS handling (CORSMiddleware + custom middleware). Custom path sets '*' when '*' in allow_origins and also sets allow-credentials=true, which is spec-invalid for cookies/auth.
Auth/security checks should be centralized to avoid contradictory CORS headers between middleware layers.
seed_data_creation: Created safe runtime draft+approval and temporary operations; cleanup executed for created operations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Business-critical bug fix verification passed: unconfirmed vehicle op saved as unconfirmed with zero journal entries; explicit آجل/unpaid still created deferred temporary journal entry; accountant listed and approved manager-created pending approval with approver != proposer. Remaining blocker is CORS credentials + wildcard origin behavior on auth endpoint.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: OPTIONS /api/auth/login with Origin header returns 204 and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Root cause is custom security middleware in backend/server.py (around lines 535-537 and 571-573) emitting '*' when '*' exists in allow_origins while credentials are enabled. Mitigation: when credentials are true, never return '*'; reflect exact allowed origin and set Vary: Origin consistently.
